70 years of CIS
Tasks that used to be extremely difficult, if not impossible, are now becoming everyday reality thanks to the magic of computer science.
For seventy years, our people have shaped the global technology revolution. From commissioning Australia’s first computer, to managing the first internet connections, we’ve seen what’s possible when the world’s greatest minds are empowered to push the boundaries of technology.

Research
CIS is home to a diverse range of researchers, specialising in Artificial intelligence, Computer Science, Human-Computer Interaction and Information Systems.

Engage

About us
CIS has been at the forefront of computing innovation in Australia for 70 years. Learn more about us and join us on our journey.
Our hope is for our students to leave here bursting with enthusiasm for the subject and with ideas that will transform the world over coming decades, with capabilities that are greatly in demand with prospective employers and the future. Our academics are continually going to places no-one has ever gone before, working in research that is both enjoyable and exciting.
Professor Uwe Aickelin, Head of School

CIS strengthens Berlin-Melbourne research collaboration
CIS researchers joined TU Berlin for a workshop advancing learning-augmented algorithms, creating new collaborations for PhD and early career researchers.

CIS PhD candidate wins FEIT Lab to Launch competition
CIS PhD candidate Xanthe Lowe-Brown won the FEIT Lab to Launch competition for MoodDJ, a music-based wellbeing platform developed through doctoral research.
28 AUG 2026
NEWS
CIS Researchers secured funding to develop cyber crisis leadership capability in Malaysia
A CIS-led project received $500,000 in DFAT funding to help strengthen cyber crisis leadership, coordination and resilience capabilities in Malaysia.
27 AUG 2026
NEWS
HCI Group celebrates success at the 2026 FEIT Excellence Awards
Several members of the Human–Computer Interaction Group were recognised at the 2026 FEIT Excellence Awards for their contributions across education, engagement, interdisciplinary research, and graduate research supervision.
